newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli economic activity shows moderate growth.
newsitem.headline: Israeli economic activity shows moderate growth.

text.p: Indicators for March-April showed relatively moderate growth in Israel's economic activity amid a slowdown in demand, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday.
The figures showed that imports of investment goods continued to decline as did tourist arrivials. The trade deficit, however, remained at a relatively low level and the rate of inflation slowed.

The bureau said industrial production rose in February- March by an annualised rate of one to three percent after declining in the four previous months. Industrial exports, including diamonds and exports to the territories, grew by an annualised three percent in April slowing from a four to five percent rate in February and March.
Imports of production inputs, not including oil, grew by an annualised rate of one to two percent in March-April turning around from the decline that had begun in February 1996.
Investment in imported machinery and equipment declined in April by an annual rate of eight percent, continuing the sharp decline that began in February 1996, the bureau said.
Building starts, as measured by floor space, declined by 19 percent in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the previous quarter and by two percent from a year earlier.

The number of salaried employees in the labour force dropped in January and February by an annual rate of five percent ending a long period of rising employment. The unemployment rate remained at about seven percent in February, similar to the rate in the previous three months, the bureau said.
The figures also showed that retail trade turnover in March declined by an annual rate of one to two percent, continuing the fall-off that started at the beginning of 1996.
Sales at retail chains rose in April by an annualised nine to 10 percent, similar to the pace in January-March.
Imports of consumer durables rose in April by an annual rate of four percent following an annualised increase of eight percent in February and March.
Merchandise exports rose by an annualised four percent in April, following a two percent annualised increase in March.
Wages rose in January-February by an annual rate of eight percent after dopping in November and December.
The consumer price index (CPI) rose in April at an annualised rate of eight to nine percent, compared with a 10 percent rate in November 1996-March 1997 period, the bureau said.
